body.claim: Derives an authorized_action from a signed tool classification fact, so a semantic identity minted from a classified tool call is re-derivable offline from signed facts plus this versioned ruleset and its pinned dependency artifacts alone. Shaped as a ruleset, not a single rule, so a later Permit-to-X is a new rule entry, not a schema change.
body.digest_convention: All digests are lowercase sha256 hex with the 'sha256:' prefix, matching every other permit-to-x artifact. base64 is used only for Ed25519 keys/signatures elsewhere, never for artifact or input digests.

profiles.serialization_note: How a logical object becomes bytes for hashing. This is the system-wide convention used by every recipe; it is NOT defined here.
profiles.payload_note: What the classification-input object contains and means. This recipe is its normative definition (see classification_input_canonicalization). Serialization and payload are separate concerns and separately named.

registered_tool.forbidden_fields: fields belonging to other (future) subject variants MUST be absent
registered_tool.unknown_kind_outcome: unsupported_derivation_subject (no_derivation, not invalid): a verifier that does not recognise the kind yields no title, it does not reject the permit.

classification_input_canonicalization.bytes: serialize the logical object with serialization_profile keel.canonical_json.payload.v1; input_digest = sha256: over those bytes. The payload_profile string is a field of the object so two different logical structures cannot canonicalize to the same bytes.
classification_input_canonicalization.purpose: Two independent verifiers computing input_digest for the same call MUST agree byte-for-byte.

identifier_grammar.equality: the verifier validates the SIGNED value directly against the grammar, then compares byte-for-byte. No case folding, Unicode normalization, whitespace trimming, alias resolution, or version stripping at verification time. The issuer produces these via normalize_known_mcp_connector_identity / normalize_mcp_tool_name and freezes them into the signed record; the verifier does not re-run or trust that normalization, it re-validates the frozen value against this grammar.
identifier_grammar.malformed: an identifier that fails the grammar makes the binding invalid, not merely unmatched.

decision_algorithm.note: The normative, ordered decision procedure. Producing an outcome is a deterministic composition of these steps, not a set of independent assertions. Steps run in order; the first that yields a terminal outcome wins, which fixes failure precedence.
steps: 1. STRUCTURAL: validate the signed record against the classification-fact schema and the subject tagged-union (required/forbidden fields for the subject kind). Malformed structure -> invalid.
2. SUBJECT KIND: if classification.subject.kind is unrecognised -> no_derivation (unsupported_derivation_subject). Stop.
3. IDENTIFIER GRAMMAR: validate every identifier against keel.registered_tool_identifiers.v1. Any failure -> invalid. Stop.

4. DEPENDENCY RESOLUTION: for each required dependency, resolve ONLY the artifact whose digest equals the permit's embedded digest. If no artifact with that exact digest is available -> unverifiable (artifact_unavailable). Stop. Possession of any other version is irrelevant and MUST NOT change this.
5. ARTIFACT INTEGRITY: if bytes offered under the embedded digest do not hash to it -> invalid (artifact corruption). Stop.
6. INTERNAL DIGEST AGREEMENT: if two signed fields required to hold the same digest disagree -> invalid. Stop.
7. INPUT DIGEST: recompute input_digest per classification_input_canonicalization; if it != classification.provenance.input.digest -> invalid. Stop.

8. RULE MATCH SET: evaluate every rule's applies_when against the same immutable facts. Let M = the set of rules whose applies_when is all-true. |M|=0 -> no_derivation (stop); |M|>1 -> invalid (stop).

9. REQUIRES: evaluate the single matched rule's `requires`. classification_registry_membership false -> no_derivation. Any digest predicate false -> invalid. control.mode != enforced_in_path -> no_derivation.

10. DERIVE: all satisfied -> valid; emit rule.derives.authorized_action. Feed it to the semantic selector as the selector's action_name/operation INPUT (an internal selector input, never a signed field named 'operation').

resolution.note: Cardinality is counted over ALL rules against the same immutable facts (step 8), never first-match. A second rule that also matched surfaces as invalid, not a silent pick.

predicate_vocabulary.classification_registry_membership: (classification.subject.connector_identity, classification.subject.canonical_tool_name) MUST be an entry in the resolved classification_registry. Absent -> no_derivation.
predicate_vocabulary.classification_registry_digest_match: classification.provenance.registry.artifact_digest MUST equal the resolved classification_registry artifact digest. Mismatch -> invalid.
predicate_vocabulary.classification_input_digest_match: classification.provenance.input.digest MUST equal the recomputed input_digest. Mismatch -> invalid.
predicate_vocabulary.closed_set: This is the entire predicate vocabulary for v1. No expression language. An unknown predicate reference -> unverifiable, never silently passed.

issuer_attested_facts.control.mode: enforced_in_path is an ISSUER-ATTESTED signed fact. An offline verifier cannot independently prove the call was intercepted in path; it verifies only that the issuer signed control.mode = enforced_in_path. This is a named trust boundary, not an independently-derived property. The whole derivation is presentation-only and non-authorizing, so relying on an issuer attestation here cannot escalate authorization; at worst a mis-attesting issuer mislabels its own record.
issuer_attested_facts.connector_identity: Operator-registered server-owned identity, issuer-attested and frozen into the signed record; the verifier re-validates its grammar but does not re-run registration.

dependencies.note: Named and normatively defined here; a verifier MUST use this definition, not infer the input shape.
System-wide serialization convention shared by every recipe; referenced, not redefined.
payment.execute -> Permit-to-Pay is unchanged from the existing presentation path.

historical_resolution.model: keel-verifier version-aware resolution (v3.7.0): resolve each dependency by the version+digest the permit embeds, NEVER by whatever is current, and NEVER substitute a different artifact that merely shares the profile name or a newer version.
historical_resolution.identity: algorithm + digest is identity; artifact_id + version are metadata and type checks only.
historical_resolution.environmental_vs_semantic: unverifiable is environmental (this verifier lacks the exact-digest artifact) and MUST resolve deterministically once the artifact is supplied. invalid/valid are semantic properties of the signed record. A verifier's local inventory of OTHER artifacts MUST NOT convert unverifiable into invalid or vice versa.

outcome_taxonomy.valid: all steps pass; authorized_action derived and fed to the selector.
outcome_taxonomy.no_derivation: rule inapplicable, subject kind unrecognised, registry entry absent, or control.mode != enforced_in_path -> generic title, permit otherwise unaffected.
outcome_taxonomy.invalid: malformed structure/identifier, digest mismatch, artifact-integrity failure, internal digest disagreement, or multiple rules match -> the semantic binding is invalid.
outcome_taxonomy.unverifiable: a required exact-digest dependency is unavailable, or an unknown predicate is referenced -> cannot decide; never treated as valid or as generic. Deterministically resolves once the missing artifact is supplied.

invariants: invocation.operation stays call.tools; authorized_action is payment.execute; these are distinct signed facts. There is no signed field named 'operation' carrying the derived action; the derivation emits ONLY authorized_action.

transport_surface and target_surface are distinct signed facts. target_surface = payment_rail is the action's resource class, not a claim the wire was a native payment-rail integration. Neither participates in rule applicability, registry lookup, classification identity, or outcome; they are orthogonal recorded facts.
control.mode == enforced_in_path is REQUIRED and issuer-attested (see issuer_attested_facts). An observed call never derives a payment authorized_action.
No provider outcome, settlement, or completion is implied. payment.execute is authority to attempt; observed_evidence carries what happened.
The classification decision bound here MUST be the same one used to enforce, bound by input_digest + registry digest, not a re-lookup that could diverge under normalization.
body.non_authorizing: This ruleset governs presentation identity only. It never affects policy evaluation, dispatch, executable authority, or verdicts. A wrong derivation degrades a title; it cannot escalate authorization.
body.conformance: The decision_algorithm plus the profile and grammar definitions are the complete contract. The test-vector corpus keel.permit.action_classification_derivation.test_vectors.v1 is MANDATORY MINIMUM evidence: every conforming verifier MUST pass it, but passing it is NECESSARY, NOT SUFFICIENT. Conformance is producing the algorithm's outcome for every well-formed input, not only for the enumerated vectors.
